game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Two dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (8 faces, each equally likely): 6, 6, 7, 7, 12, 12, 12, 12.
- Die 2 (4 faces, each equally likely): 1, 1, 6, 7.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
Fair value before any reveal is 13 (die 1 averages 9.25, die 2 averages 3.75), and the settlement distribution is symmetric about it: 7, 8, 12, 13, 14, 18, 19.

With alpha unknown (prior mean about 0.48), tight quotes lose too much to informed traders on the 18/19 and 7/8 outcomes. Expected profit per side peaks at roughly 0.107 anywhere from 18 to 19 on the ask, and symmetrically 8 to 7 on the bid.

I am quoting just inside 18 and 8. That costs about 0.005 per side in expectation, but an informed trader then trades on any of the four extreme outcomes instead of two. This makes the round's settlement more informative about alpha, which matters for how tight to quote in later rounds.

{"bid": 8.1, "ask": 17.9}

Fair value is 13 (die 1 mean 9.25 + die 2 mean 3.75), and the sum distribution is symmetric about 13: 7 and 8 (1/8 each), 12 (1/16), 13 (3/8), 14 (1/16), 18 and 19 (1/8 each).

The no-trade at 8.1 / 17.9 shifts belief towards lower alpha (posterior about 0.41 / 0.33 / 0.26 for 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9, mean alpha about 0.42) and towards the middle sums, but by symmetry the fair value stays at 13.

For the ask, I weighed noise-trader edge against the loss to an informed buyer holding 18 or 19:

| Ask | Noise edge | Informed loss | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15.0 | 0.316 | 0.142 | 0.174 |
| 16.0 | 0.316 | 0.101 | 0.215 |
| 16.2 | 0.308 | 0.093 | 0.215 |
| 17.0 | 0.262 | 0.061 | 0.201 |
| 18.0 | 0.188 | 0.020 | 0.168 |

The optimum is around 16.2, and the bid mirrors it at 9.8.

{"bid": 9.8, "ask": 16.2}

**Posterior after the reveal.** With die 2 = 6, the settlement is 12, 13 or 18 (prior 1/4, 1/4, 1/2). The no-trade at 17.9 and the buy at 16.2 shift weight towards 18: I get P(18) ≈ 0.68 and P(12) ≈ P(13) ≈ 0.16, so the public fair value is about 16.3.

**Ask.** Any ask below 18 gets lifted by an informed trader whenever the value is 18, so I quote at or above 18, where only noise traders buy. Expected profit is nearly flat between 18.4 and 18.6 (about 0.40 per quote), so I take 18.5.

**Bid.** An informed trader only sells when the value is 12 or 13, and only if my bid is above that value. A bid of 13.0 is exposed only to the value-12 case (about 4% chance of losing 1) while still buying from noise traders well below fair value. Expected profit is about 0.27, roughly flat between 12.5 and 13.0, and it falls off above 13.

{"bid": 13.0, "ask": 18.5}

Die 2 = 6, so the contract settles at 12, 13 or 18. From the history (no trade at 8.1/17.9, a buy at 16.2, no trade at 13/18.5) my approximate posterior is about 76% on 18, 15% on 13 and 9% on 12, giving a fair value near 16.7.

- **Ask:** any ask at 18 or above is safe from informed buyers, since no settlement exceeds 18. Against noise traders, expected profit peaks at about 19.2.
- **Bid:** a bid of exactly 13 is only hit by an informed seller when settlement is 12, which is now unlikely. It beats both 12 and 14 on expected profit.

{"bid": 13.0, "ask": 19.2}

Sum distribution: 7 (1/8), 8 (1/8), 12 (1/16), 13 (3/8), 14 (1/16), 18 (1/8), 19 (1/8), so the fair value is 13.

Round 1 (an informed-looking buy at 16.2 ahead of an 18 settlement, plus three no-trades) leaves my posterior on alpha at roughly 0.23 / 0.54 / 0.24 for 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9, so a mean near 0.5.

With that much informed flow, quoting inside the 18/19 and 7/8 tails loses more to informed traders than it earns from noise: an ask of 16.2 is about −0.01 expected per quote. Quoting at 18 or 19 earns about +0.10. I pick 8 / 18, which only loses to the extreme outcomes (7 or 19) and still collects a wide edge from noise traders.

{"bid": 8, "ask": 18}

With die 2 = 6, the contract settles at 12, 13 or 18 (probabilities 0.25, 0.25, 0.5), so the fair value is 15.25.

- **Ask 18:** an informed trader never buys here, because no settlement value is above 18. Noise traders still buy about 20% of the time, at an edge of 2.75, which is close to the best achievable against noise alone. Any lower ask loses to an informed trader whenever the value is 18.
- **Bid 12:** an informed trader never sells here, because no settlement value is below 12. Noise traders sell about 16% of the time, at an edge of 3.25. Raising the bid towards 13 gains only a little from noise and loses to informed traders when the value is 12; my rough estimate from the history puts the informed share near 0.5, so that is not worth it.

{"bid": 12, "ask": 18}

Die 2 = 6 leaves settlement at 12, 13 or 18 with probabilities 1/4, 1/4, 1/2, so fair value is 15.25. No trade so far this round tells us anything about die 1, because an informed trader would not trade at any of the quotes posted.

- **Ask 18.0:** an informed trader never buys here, since the value is at most 18. A noise trader buys about 20% of the time, giving me an edge of 2.75. Going lower exposes me to informed buying when the value is 18; going higher earns less from noise.
- **Bid 12.0:** an informed trader never sells here, since the value is at least 12. A noise trader sells about 16% of the time, giving me an edge of 3.25. Raising the bid to 13 gains little from noise and loses to informed sellers when the value is 12, which matters because the history so far points to a fairly high informed share (roughly 0.5 to 0.6 on average).

{"bid": 12.0, "ask": 18.0}

Fair value before any reveal is 13 (die 1 mean 9.25 + die 2 mean 3.75), with possible sums 7, 8, 12, 13, 14, 18, 19, symmetric around 13.

From the history so far, my rough posterior on alpha leans high (about 0.12 / 0.52 / 0.36 on 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9, mean near 0.6). The round 1 buy at 16.2 before an 18 settlement is the main evidence.

At that level of informed flow, any quote inside the extreme outcomes loses more to informed traders than it earns from noise traders. For example, an ask at 16 expects about -0.37 from informed against +0.22 from noise. Quoting at the extremes (7 and 19) cannot be picked off, since an informed trader only trades on a strict inequality, and it still collects about 6 of edge from the occasional noise trader. I estimate that at roughly +0.085 per side, better than 18.5 or 20.

**Reasoning:** The sum takes values 7, 8 (1/8 each), 12 (1/16), 13 (3/8), 14 (1/16), 18, 19 (1/8 each), so fair value is 13.

From the session so far, the informed share looks high. The round 1 purchase at 16.2 before an 18 settlement, plus the long run of no-trades at wide quotes, gives a rough posterior on alpha of about 0.12 / 0.52 / 0.37 for 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9, with a mean near 0.6.

At that level, any ask below 19 or bid above 7 loses more to informed traders than it earns from noise traders:

| Ask | Expected profit per quote |
|---|---|
| 16 | about -0.15 |
| 18 | about +0.05 |
| 19 | about +0.08 |

Quoting at the extremes of the support (7 and 19) means an informed trader can never profit against me, while I still collect a large edge on the occasional noise trade. The bid side is symmetric.

From the session so far, my rough posterior on alpha is about 0.11 / 0.51 / 0.38 for 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9, so roughly 60% of counterparties are informed. The round 1 buy at 16.2 ahead of an 18 settlement is the main evidence.

With that much informed flow, the best quotes sit exactly at the extreme outcomes:

- **Ask 19:** an informed trader never buys, since no settlement value is above 19. A noise trader buys about 20% of the time, and I earn 2.75 of edge on each such sale.
- **Bid 13:** an informed trader never sells, since no settlement value is below 13. A noise trader sells about 16% of the time, and I earn 3.25 of edge on each such purchase.

Tightening either side (e.g. ask 18 or bid 14) lets informed traders pick me off and lowers expected profit at this alpha estimate.

{"bid": 13, "ask": 19}

Die 2 = 7, so settlement is 13, 14 or 19 (probabilities 1/4, 1/4, 1/2), giving a fair value of 16.25.

- **Ask 19:** an informed trader never buys here, since no value is above 19. A noise trader buys about 20% of the time, at an edge of 2.75. Going lower lets the informed pick me off whenever the value is 19.
- **Bid 13:** an informed trader never sells here, since no value is below 13. A noise trader sells about 16% of the time, at an edge of 3.25. Raising the bid towards 14 gains almost nothing from noise traders and loses to the informed when the value is 13.

The session so far points to a high informed share (my rough estimate of alpha averages about 0.6), so staying on the edges of the value range is worth more than tightening.

{"bid": 13, "ask": 19}

Fair value is still 13: the sale at 7 must have come from a noise trader, since an informed trader never sells at 7 when the lowest possible settlement is 7. So it carries no information about this round's value.

From the session so far, my rough posterior on alpha is about 0.18 / 0.68 / 0.14 for 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9, a mean near 0.48.

At that alpha, quoting at 8 and 18 earns about 0.11 per side per quote. Tighter quotes lose more to informed traders at the extreme sums (7, 8, 18, 19) than they gain from noise traders, and 7/19 is marginally worse. The +1 position does not change this, as the limit of 5 is far away.

{"bid": 8, "ask": 18}

Die 2 = 1, so settlement is 7, 8 or 13 (die 1 = 6, 7 or 12).

- **Fair value:** no one sold at my 8 bid last quote, which slightly lowers the chance of a 7. I put the odds at roughly 14% / 29% / 57% for 7 / 8 / 13, giving a fair value of about 10.7.
- **Ask:** at 13 or above an informed trader never buys, so only noise traders lift it. The expected edge is nearly flat between 13 and 13.5, so I pick 13.1.
- **Bid:** at 7 or below an informed trader never sells. Bidding up to 8 gains a little more noise flow but gets hit by an informed trader when the value is 7, so 7 is marginally best.

{"bid": 7, "ask": 13.1}

Die 2 = 1, so the contract settles at 7, 8 or 13. The no-trade at my bid of 8 in quote 2 makes 7 somewhat less likely, so I put the fair value at roughly 10.6.

- **Ask 13.1:** an informed trader never buys here, since the value cannot exceed 13. Only noise traders lift it, at about 2.5 above fair, which is close to the profit-maximising distance for noise with standard deviation 3.3.
- **Bid 7:** an informed trader never sells here, since the value cannot be below 7. Only noise traders hit it, at about 3.6 below fair. Raising the bid to 8 gains more noise flow but exposes me to informed selling when the value is 7, and the two roughly cancel.

Both sides are therefore free of adverse selection and earn only from noise traders.

At alpha ≈ 0.4, expected profit per quote on the ask side is:

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 16 | 0.08 |
| 17 | 0.12 |
| 17.9 | 0.14 |
| 18 | 0.145 |
| 18.5 | 0.13 |
| 19 | 0.12 |

An ask of 18 is best: it only loses to an informed trader when the sum is 19, and still earns 5 from noise traders. The bid side mirrors this at 8.

{"bid": 8, "ask": 18}

Fair value before the reveal is 13 (die 1 mean 9.25 + die 2 mean 3.75), with settlement values 7, 8, 12, 13, 14, 18, 19 symmetric around it.

From the session so far, my posterior on alpha is roughly 0.28 / 0.69 / 0.03 for 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9, so about 0.39 in expectation. The two trades in round 4 went the wrong way for an informed trader, which makes 0.9 very unlikely.

Expected profit per side at that alpha, comparing ask levels (the bid is the mirror image):

|---|---|---|---|

| 18 | 0.20 | 0.05 | 0.15 |
| 19 | 0.13 | 0.00 | 0.13 |

Quoting at 8 / 18 is best: an informed trader only picks me off when the value is 7 or 19, and then only for 1.

From the session history, alpha = 0.5 looks most likely (about 0.69), with 0.05 at about 0.28 and 0.9 nearly ruled out by the two round-4 trades that an informed trader would not have made.

- **Ask:** at 13 or above an informed trader never buys, so the ask only faces noise traders. Expected profit peaks around 13.0–13.5, so I quote 13.2.
- **Bid:** at 8 an informed trader sells only if settlement is 7, which is unlikely and costs just 1. That small risk is outweighed by the extra noise flow compared with bidding 7. Bidding above 8 exposes me to informed selling at 8 as well, which is not worth it.

No sale at my 8 bid across three quotes this round makes 7 somewhat less likely, so I put fair value at roughly 10.3–11.1.

**Informed share:** two of my three fills (the sale at 7 in a round that settled at 8, the purchase at 13.1 in a round that settled at 8) cannot have been informed, and an informed trader would have lifted my 17.9 ask in round 1 quote 1. | Ask | Expected profit |

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Four dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 1, 3, 4, 5, 8.
- Die 2 (8 faces, each equally likely): 0, 2, 3, 3, 5, 5, 10, 11.
- Die 3 (8 faces, each equally likely): 1, 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 9, 12.
- Die 4 (6 faces, each equally likely): 0, 1, 3, 5, 9, 10.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
Prior fair value is about 18.6 (die means 3.67 + 4.88 + 5.38 + 4.67), with a standard deviation near 6.9. The sale at 12.1 is fairly likely to have been informed (roughly 55–57% by my estimate), which would put the sum at 12 or below. That pulls the fair value down to roughly 13–13.5.

With the average informed share now near 0.5, I keep both sides wide:

- **Bid 7.0:** far enough below fair that noise sellers pay more than informed sellers cost.
- **Ask 24.5:** about break-even at any level from 20 up, so I keep it high to limit losses to informed buyers.

{"bid": 7.0, "ask": 24.5}

**Fair value after the reveal.** With die 1 = 1, the unconditional expected sum is about 15.9, but the earlier sale at 12.1 and the no-trade at 7 / 24.5 pull it down. Weighting the three possible alpha values by how well they explain those two events, I estimate the public fair value at about 11.5, with most of the informed-trader mass on sums of 7 to 12. These are hand-computed approximations, not exact.

**Quote choice.** The posterior leans toward high alpha (roughly 0.23 / 0.34 / 0.43 on 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9), so I keep both sides wide and place each just outside the bulk of informed flow.

- **Bid 7.0:** an informed seller only hits this if the sum is 6 or less, which is unlikely, while noise traders still sell there about 22% of the time. Raising the bid above 7 would let the heavily weighted sums of 7 to 12 sell to me.
- **Ask 18.0:** an informed buyer only lifts this if the sum is 19 or more. This was the best of the asks I checked between 17 and 24; an ask near 13 loses money to informed buyers.

Expected edge is roughly 0.5 on the bid and 0.2 on the ask.

{"bid": 7.0, "ask": 18.0}

Die 1 = 1 gives a naive fair value of about 15.9, but the session history pulls it lower. The sale at 12.1 followed by two no-trades inside 7–18 puts most posterior weight on a settlement between 7 and 12 and on a high informed share (about 0.6). My estimate of the public fair value is about 11.1.

- **Bid 7:** an informed seller only hits this if the sum is below 7, which is unlikely, while noise sellers still trade at a good price. Raising the bid into the 7–12 range would expose it to the bulk of the informed mass.
- **Ask 17.5:** expected profit is roughly flat between 17 and 18, since the remaining informed risk above that is small and noise buyers pay well above fair value.

{"bid": 7, "ask": 17.5}

Fair value before any reveal is the sum of the die means: 3.67 + 4.88 + 5.38 + 4.67 ≈ 18.6, with a standard deviation of about 6.9.

Round 1 suggests the informed share is still very uncertain: the first sale at 12.1 fits an informed trader (settlement was 11), but the sale at 7 could only have been noise. My rough posterior puts about half the weight on alpha = 0.5 and the rest split evenly between 0.05 and 0.9, so the expected alpha is about 0.5.

At that level, a rough normal approximation puts the best quote about 8 away from fair value on each side. The dice have a fatter upper tail, so I set the ask slightly wider than the bid.

{"bid": 11, "ask": 27}

game.title: Card sum
game.description: A custom deck of 22 cards is shuffled: 4 cards worth 0, 1 card worth 2, 4 cards worth 3, 1 card worth 6, 4 cards worth 7, 4 cards worth 11, 4 cards worth 15. 2 cards are dealt face down, without replacement.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of the dealt cards' values.

info.raw:
Fair value is the expected sum of two cards: 2 × 152/22 ≈ 13.8, with possible sums running from 0 to 30.

With alpha unknown (average about 0.48), tight quotes lose to informed traders, so I quote wide. Using the exact sum distribution, the best ask sits just under 22 and the best bid around 6 to 7, each earning roughly 0.16 to 0.20 per quote in expectation.

I place the quotes just inside the sums 22 and 7. That costs almost nothing, but it means an informed trader would trade on those sums too, which tells me more about alpha once the round settles.

That puts roughly 62% on the seller having been informed, so the updated fair value is about 8.0 and the weight on high alpha has risen.

- **Bid 2.0:** only a sum of 0 lets an informed trader hit it, while noise traders centred near 8 still sell about 17% of the time. This has the best expected profit of the bids I checked (about +0.5).
- **Ask 17.0:** lower asks get picked off by informed buyers on the remaining high-sum cases. At 17.0 the noise-trader edge slightly outweighs that loss (about +0.06), and a sale would also flatten my long position.

{"bid": 2.0, "ask": 17.0}

Card 1 = 3, so settlement is 3 + card 2, with possible values 3, 5, 6, 9, 10, 14, 18 (prior mean about 10.1). My approximate posterior puts about 85% on settlement being 3, 5 or 6, with a fair value near 5.7.

**Bid:** 3.0 is the highest bid an informed trader can never hit, because the settlement is never below 3. Any fill there is a noise trader, worth about 0.8 in expectation; bidding 4 or 5 lets informed sellers in when the total is 3 and is worse.

game.title: Urn of unknown mix
game.description: An urn holds 11 balls, each red or blue. Each ball was independently painted red with probability 0.3. 2 balls are drawn without replacement. Revealed draws show 1 for red and 0 for blue.
game.contract: The contract settles at 10 times the number of red balls originally in the urn.

info.raw:

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Four dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (4 faces, each equally likely): 2, 7, 10, 11.
- Die 2 (4 faces, each equally likely): 0, 3, 4, 6.
- Die 3 (6 faces, each equally likely): 0, 1, 6, 9, 10, 10.
- Die 4 (4 faces, each equally likely): 0, 1, 2, 7.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

- Die 1 (8 faces, each equally likely): 1, 3, 3, 5, 5, 6, 6, 9.
- Die 2 (6 faces, each equally likely): 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, 11.

game.title: Coin of unknown bias
game.description: A coin is picked at random from a set of coins: P(heads) = 0.1 with probability 2/5, P(heads) = 0.2 with probability 3/10, P(heads) = 0.6 with probability 3/10. The coin is not shown. It is flipped 7 times. Revealed flips show 1 for heads and 0 for tails.
game.contract: The contract settles at the number of heads in all flips.

info.raw:
Prior fair value is 7 × 0.28 = 1.96 heads, with a long right tail from the 0.6 coin.

- **Bid 0.8:** an informed seller only hits it when the settlement is 0 (about 25% of rounds), so it is roughly break-even at the average alpha and clearly profitable if alpha is low. It also tells me something about alpha.
- **Ask 4.0:** an informed buyer only lifts it at 5+ heads (about 13%). This is slightly negative at the average alpha, but it is a cheap way to learn alpha on the ask side; an ask of 3.0 would cost about three times as much in expectation.

Fair value before any reveal is about 1.96 heads (mean bias 0.28 × 7 flips), and after the no-trade at 0.8 / 4 it is roughly 2.0.

- **Ask 4:** an informed buyer only lifts this when the settlement is 5 or more (about 7% likely), and the edge of 2 over fair against noise buyers slightly outweighs that loss. Asks nearer 3 lose money once the 4-heads outcomes are included.
- **Bid 0.3:** an informed seller only hits this when the settlement is 0, where I lose just 0.3, while noise sellers give me about 1.7 of edge. Expected profit is nearly flat for bids between 0 and 0.5, so I take a low one to limit the informed loss.

The settlement is a whole number of at least 1, and informed traders are likely common (posterior mean alpha about 0.5), so I quote at the integer edges:

game.title: Urn of unknown mix
game.description: An urn holds 7 balls, each red or blue. The number of red balls is equally likely to be any of 0, 1, ..., 7. 4 balls are drawn without replacement. Revealed draws show 1 for red and 0 for blue.
game.contract: The contract settles at 10 times the number of red balls originally in the urn.

info.raw:
Before any reveal the settlement is uniform on 0, 10, ..., 70, so fair value is 35.

The right spread depends heavily on the unknown alpha:

- **If alpha is 0.05**, a quote about 16 either side of fair earns roughly 4.5 per quote from noise traders.
- **If alpha is 0.5 or 0.9**, the same quote loses to informed traders (about 1 and 6 per quote respectively), and only very wide quotes are safe.

Averaged over the three alphas, quoting 19/51 costs about 0.7 in expectation on this quote. I accept that as the price of learning alpha early: once the round settles, whether each trade was on the right side of the settlement value separates informed from noise flow quickly, and there are 23 quotes left to use that.

{"bid": 19, "ask": 51}

Given one red and one blue draw, the red count is weighted R(7−R) over 1–6, so the fair value is 35 and the distribution is symmetric (the two no-trade quotes thin out the 10 and 60 tails but keep it symmetric).

I compared asks by expected profit for this quote across the three possible informed fractions, weighted by their posterior after two no-trades (roughly 0.26 / 0.32 / 0.42 for 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9):

| Ask | Expected profit (ask side) |
|---|---|
| 45 | about 0.51 |
| 49 | about 1.02 |
| 50 | about 1.12 |

An ask of 50 is best because an informed trader only lifts it when the value is 60, which is now unlikely, while noise traders still pay 15 over fair. Wider asks (52, 55) earn less from noise. By symmetry the bid is 20.

Quoting 20/50 also tells me more about the informed fraction than 21/49: a trade here is likely if informed traders are rare and very unlikely if they are common.

{"bid": 20, "ask": 50}

After one red and one blue, the posterior on the number of red balls is symmetric around 3.5, so fair value is 35, with settlement most likely 20, 30, 40 or 50.

Three quotes with no trade point towards a high informed share (my estimate is about 60% informed on average), and make 10 and 60 unlikely (about 2% each).

- **Ask 50 / bid 20:** an informed trader only trades against me if the value is 60 or 10, which is rare, while noise traders still pay me 15 of edge. Expected profit is about 1.0 per side.
- **Tighter quotes (e.g. 45 or 40):** these get picked off whenever the value is 50 (about 22% likely), which costs more than the extra noise flow earns.
- **Wider quotes (e.g. 55 or 60):** these are safe but lose too much noise flow.

So I keep the same quote.

{"bid": 20, "ask": 50}

**Quote: bid 0, ask 70.**

Before any draw is revealed the value is uniform on 0, 10, ..., 70, so the fair value is 35.

Round 1 gave four no-trades at roughly 20/50 with settlement 50. An informed trader would never have traded there, while a noise trader would have traded about a third of the time. That shifts the weights on alpha from one third each to roughly 0.14 (alpha 0.05), 0.31 (alpha 0.5) and 0.55 (alpha 0.9), so the expected alpha is about 0.66.

Expected profit per quote on the ask side under those weights (the bid side is symmetric):

| Ask | Loss to informed | Gain from noise | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 51 | −2.30 | +0.87 | −1.43 |
| 61 | −0.74 | +0.46 | −0.28 |
| 65 | −0.41 | +0.31 | −0.10 |
| 69 | −0.08 | +0.20 | +0.11 |
| 70 | 0 | +0.17 | +0.17 |

At 0/70 an informed trader can never trade, since the value cannot be above 70 or below 0, so any fill is a noise trader at a 35-point edge. A fill there would also be clean evidence that alpha is low.

I considered quoting tighter to learn alpha faster. A round at 20/50 costs about 12 to 13 in expectation, and the payoff from discovering alpha is 0.05 is worth about 10 at best, so it does not pay.

{"bid": 0, "ask": 70}

Four no-trades in round 1 (where an informed trader would not have traded at a settlement of 50, but a noise trader often would) shift my belief towards high alpha: roughly 0.13 / 0.30 / 0.56 for alpha = 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9.

With nothing revealed, the value is uniform on 0 to 70 with fair value 35. At that belief, any ask below 70 or bid above 0 loses more to informed traders than it earns from noise traders. For example, 10/60 is about -0.7 per quote in expectation against about +0.3 for 0/70. Quoting 0/70 can never lose, since the value cannot be outside that range, and still collects from extreme noise traders.

Tightening now to learn alpha would cost about 4.5 per quote in expectation, which is not clearly repaid over the remaining quotes. Stage 2 is the cheaper place to tighten, once the draws narrow the range.

{"bid": 0, "ask": 70}

**Fair value.** After two red draws, the posterior weight on R red balls is proportional to R(R−1), giving settlement probabilities 70: 0.375, 60: 0.268, 50: 0.179, 40: 0.107, 30: 0.054, 20: 0.018. The fair value is 57.5.

**Alpha.** Six quotes with no trade favour a high informed share: the posterior is roughly 0.13 / 0.30 / 0.57 on alpha = 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9, so I quote defensively.

**Ask 70.** The settlement can never exceed 70, so an informed trader never buys here. Only noise traders lift it (about 22% of the time), each at a 12.5 edge, so it is risk-free profit.

**Bid 30.** An informed trader only sells here when the settlement is 20 (probability 0.018), costing 10. Noise traders hit it about 4% of the time at a 27.5 edge. Averaged over the alpha posterior this is worth about 0.30, better than a bid of 40 (about 0.20) or 20 (about 0.12).

{"bid": 30, "ask": 70}

Two reds drawn gives a posterior on the red count proportional to R(R-1), so the value is 20, 30, 40, 50, 60 or 70 with weights 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, 42 out of 112, and the fair value is 57.5.

Seven quotes with no trade point towards a high informed share: my rough posterior on alpha is about 0.11 / 0.29 / 0.60 for 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9, a mean near 0.69.

- **Ask 70:** an informed trader never buys here, since the value cannot exceed 70, while a noise trader buys about 22% of the time at an edge of 12.5. Lower asks lose to the 37.5% chance the value is 70; higher asks earn slightly less from noise.
- **Bid 30:** an informed trader sells only if the value is 20 (2/112), costing little, while noise still gives a small positive edge. Bids at 40 or 50 lose more to informed sellers than they earn at this alpha.

{"bid": 30, "ask": 70}

**Reading the history:** all 8 earlier quotes produced no trade, and in each case an informed trader would not have traded (settlement was inside my quotes), while a noise trader would have traded about 3% to 35% of the time. That shifts the posterior on alpha from 1/3 each to roughly 0.09 (alpha 0.05), 0.27 (alpha 0.5) and 0.64 (alpha 0.9), so expected alpha is about 0.72.

**This quote:** nothing is revealed, so the value is uniform on 0, 10, ..., 70 with fair value 35. Expected profit per side for a few asks (the bid is symmetric):

| Ask | Informed loss | Noise gain | Net at expected alpha 0.72 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50 | large (buys at 60 and 70) | 2.61 × (1 − alpha) | about −1.9 |
| 60 | 1.25 × alpha | 1.48 × (1 − alpha) | about −0.48 |
| 65 | 0.625 × alpha | 0.91 × (1 − alpha) | about −0.19 |
| 70 | 0 | 0.50 × (1 − alpha) | about +0.14 |

An ask of 70 (and a bid of 0) cannot be picked off by an informed trader and still collects 35 of edge from the occasional extreme noise trader. Tightening only pays if alpha is 0.05, which now has under 10% probability, and testing for it with a 20/50 quote would cost about 4 in expectation per quote. I stay wide.

{"bid": 0, "ask": 70}

**Fair value.** With two reds drawn, the posterior on the red count R is proportional to R(R−1), so values 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70 have weights 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, 42 out of 112. The fair value is 57.5.

**Informed share.** Ten quotes without a trade, with settlements of 50 and 60 that an informed trader would not have traded on, point to a high alpha. My posterior is roughly 0.08 / 0.27 / 0.65 on 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9, a mean near 0.72.

**Ask.** At 70 an informed trader never buys, since the value cannot exceed 70. A noise trader buys about 22% of the time, for an edge of 12.5. Any lower ask lets the informed trader pick me off when the value is 70 (probability 0.375), and that is worse at every alpha. A higher ask gains edge but loses more in trade frequency, so 70 is the best ask.

**Bid.** Expected profit per quote at alpha 0.72:

| Bid | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 20 | 0.10 |
| 30 | 0.20 |
| 35 | 0.12 |
| 40 | 0.03 |

At 30 the only informed loss is when the value is 20 (probability 0.018), so 30 is the best bid.

{"bid": 30, "ask": 70}

After two red draws, the posterior on the number of red balls (2 to 7) is weighted 2 : 6 : 12 : 20 : 30 : 42, so the fair value is 57.5 and settlement lies between 20 and 70.

Eleven quotes without a trade point towards a high share of informed traders: my posterior on alpha is roughly 7% / 25% / 68% for 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9, a mean of about 0.74.

- **Ask 70:** an informed trader can never buy here, since settlement cannot exceed 70. A noise trader buys about 22% of the time, at an edge of 12.5. Lower asks expose me to the 37.5% chance that settlement is 70, and higher asks only lose noise flow.
- **Bid 30:** an informed trader sells only if settlement is 20 (probability 2/112), costing 10. A noise trader sells about 4% of the time, at an edge of 27.5. A bid of 40 picks up more noise flow but loses too much to informed sellers at this alpha, and a bid of 20 gives away most of the noise edge.

{"bid": 30, "ask": 70}

**Reasoning:** Before any draws are revealed, the settlement value is uniform on {0, 10, ..., 70}, so the fair value is 35.

Thirteen quotes without a single trade point to a high informed share. Updating the three alpha values on that record gives roughly 0.71 for alpha = 0.9, 0.24 for alpha = 0.5 and 0.05 for alpha = 0.05.

At those odds, tightening the quote loses money. An ask of 60 earns about 0.36 from noise traders but gives up about 0.95 to informed traders when the value is 70. An ask of 70 and a bid of 0 can never be hit by an informed trader, and still earn a little from extreme noise valuations (about 0.12 per side per quote).

Tighter quotes would only pay if alpha were 0.05, and that is too unlikely to be worth testing.

{"bid": 0, "ask": 70}

**Fair value:** after draws 0 and 1, the red count is 1 to 6 with weights proportional to R(7−R), i.e. 6, 10, 12, 12, 10, 6 out of 56. The mean is 3.5 reds, so fair value is 35, with settlement between 10 and 60.

**Alpha:** 14 quotes with no trades shift the posterior towards a high informed share, roughly 0.19 / 0.33 / 0.49 on 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9, for an expected alpha of about 0.61.

**Quote:** at that alpha, any ask below 60 loses more to informed traders than it earns from noise traders. Expected profit per quote on the ask side is about 0.37 at 50, 0.50 at 55 and 0.58 at 60, then falls again above 60. At 60 an informed trader can never profit against me, and noise traders still buy about 6% of the time at 25 over fair. The bid side is symmetric, so the bid is 10.

{"bid": 10, "ask": 60}

**Fair value:** with one red and one blue in two draws, the posterior on the number of red balls is proportional to R(7−R), giving weights 6, 10, 12, 12, 10, 6 on R = 1..6. The mean is 3.5, so fair value is 35 and settlement lies in 10..60.

**Alpha:** fifteen quotes with no trade, none of which an informed trader would have hit, shift the posterior towards high alpha. I get roughly 0.05 / 0.23 / 0.72 on alpha = 0.05 / 0.5 / 0.9, a mean of about 0.76.

**Quote choice:** an informed trader only buys if the value is strictly above the ask, so an ask of 60 is never hit by one. Against noise traders it earns about 0.24 × P(noise > 60) × 25 ≈ 0.36. Tightening loses money on balance: at 55 the expected profit falls to about 0.10, and at 50 it is negative, because the 6/56 chance of a 60 settlement gets picked off. Widening to 61 also earns less (about 0.33). The bid side is symmetric, so 10 is best there.

{"bid": 10, "ask": 60}

Two reds revealed, so the posterior on the red count is proportional to R(R-1): fair value is 57.5, with P(70) = 37.5%, P(60) = 26.8%, P(50) = 17.9%, P(40) = 10.7%, P(30) = 5.4%, P(20) = 1.8%.

Eighteen quotes without a trade shift the posterior on alpha heavily towards 0.9 (roughly 74% on 0.9, 21% on 0.5, 4% on 0.05), so expected alpha is about 0.78.

- **Ask 70:** an informed trader never buys here, since the value cannot exceed 70. Noise traders buy about 22% of the time at an edge of 12.5, which is the best available; any lower ask is picked off when the value is 70.
- **Bid 30:** an informed trader only sells here when the value is 20 (1.8%). The noise edge of 27.5 slightly outweighs that, and both higher and lower bids come out worse in expectation.

{"bid": 30, "ask": 70}

**Fair value:** after two red draws, the posterior on the number of reds is proportional to R(R−1), which gives a mean of 5.75 reds, so the fair value is 57.5.

**Informed share:** 19 quotes without a trade is far more likely when most counterparties are informed, since my quotes have never been on the wrong side of the settlement value. My rough posterior puts about 77% on alpha = 0.9, 20% on 0.5 and 3% on 0.05, so expected alpha is about 0.79.

**Ask 70:** the value cannot exceed 70, so an informed trader never lifts this ask. A noise trader lifts it about 22% of the time for an edge of 12.5, and going lower exposes me to the 37.5% chance that the value is 70.

**Bid 30:** an informed trader only hits it when the value is 20 (about 1.8% chance, loss 10). A noise trader hits it about 4% of the time for an edge of 27.5. That nets slightly positive, and bids of 29, 31 or 40 come out worse.

{"bid": 30, "ask": 70}

Twenty quotes without a trade point strongly to a high share of informed counterparties (my posterior is roughly 79% on alpha = 0.9, 18% on 0.5, 3% on 0.05). With nothing revealed, fair value is 35 and settlement is uniform on 0, 10, ..., 70. Any quote inside the 0–70 range loses more to informed traders than it earns from noise traders. For example, an ask of 69 gives up about 0.10 to an informed buyer when the value is 70 and gains only about 0.01 more from noise than an ask of 70. Quoting at the extremes cannot be picked off and still collects a small edge from extreme noise traders.

At 60 the informed trader can never buy (settlement never exceeds 60), so the only fills are noise traders paying 25 over fair. The same logic puts the bid at 10.

game.description: An urn holds 10 balls, each red or blue. Each ball was independently painted red with probability 0.6. 4 balls are drawn without replacement. Revealed draws show 1 for red and 0 for blue.
game.contract: The contract settles at the number of red balls originally in the urn.

info.raw:
After the buy at 7, the public fair value moves up to about 7.07, because the buyer may have been informed (settlement 8 or more).

- **Ask:** 8, 8.5, 8.9 and 9 all come out at roughly +0.04 expected profit. I pick 9 because only a settlement of exactly 10 can hurt me there, while noise traders still occasionally lift it.
- **Bid:** every level from 4 to 7 has negative expected profit. A bid of 5 is nearly free (about -0.007) and a fill there would tell me something about alpha for the remaining rounds, so I keep it.

{"bid": 5, "ask": 9}

Posterior after the two red draws, the buy at 7 and the no-trade at 5/9 puts fair value near 7.76, with most of the mass on 8 and 9 red balls and a high chance that informed traders are common.

- **Ask 9.0:** an informed buyer only lifts this if the urn has 10 reds (about 1% likely), while noise traders still lift it about 13% of the time. Expected edge is about +0.09, better than nearby asks.
- **Bid 6.0:** bids of 7 or more lose to informed sellers. At 6.0 only urns with 5 or fewer reds hurt, for a small positive edge of about +0.02.

{"bid": 6.0, "ask": 9.0}

**Fair value now:** two red draws give a base of 2 + 8 × 0.6 = 6.8, but the trade history pushes it higher. The buy at 7 before the reveal, followed by two no-trades at 5/9 and 6/9, makes a high informed share likely and concentrates the settlement on 8 or 9. My posterior mean is about 7.85, with roughly 54% on 8 and 23% on 9.

**Ask at 9:** an informed buyer only lifts this if the urn holds 10 reds (under 1%), while a noise buyer pays well above fair value. Lower asks such as 8.5 get picked off whenever the value is 9, which costs more than the extra noise flow earns.

**Bid at 6.3:** a bid near 7 or 8 loses to informed sellers when the value is 6 or 7, and noise sellers are more likely in the low-informed-share case where the value is lower. Bids between 6 and 6.5 all earn a small positive edge, so I sit in the middle of that range.

{"bid": 6.3, "ask": 9}

Before any reveal, the urn's red count is Binomial(10, 0.6), so the fair value is 6.

Round 1 says the informed share is probably low. The buy at 7 and the non-trade at my 6.3 bid (an informed trader knowing 6 would have sold there) both had to come from noise traders. My rough posterior is about 74% on alpha 0.05, 25% on 0.5 and 1% on 0.9, a mean near 0.17.

At that mix, quoting exactly on the integers one away from fair is best: an ask of 7 earns about 0.11 expected per quote, slightly more than 6.9 or 7.2, and the bid at 5 is similar. Sitting exactly on 5 and 7 also means an informed trader with value 5 or 7 does not trade.

{"bid": 5, "ask": 7}

Prior value is Binomial(10, 0.6), so the fair value is 6 with nothing revealed and no trade last quote.

Round 1 suggests alpha is probably low: the buyer at 7 (settlement 6) and the non-seller at 6.3 were both noise traders. That puts roughly 74% on alpha = 0.05, 25% on 0.5 and 1% on 0.9, for an expected alpha of about 0.17.

game.title: Urn of unknown mix
game.description: An urn holds 10 balls, each red or blue. The number of red balls is equally likely to be any of 0, 1, ..., 10. 2 balls are drawn without replacement. Revealed draws show 1 for red and 0 for blue.
game.contract: The contract settles at the number of red balls originally in the urn.
